setup.step1Description: OBS WebSocket is required for Church Hub to control OBS Studio. For OBS 28+, it's built-in. For older versions, download and install it:
setup.step2Instruction2: Go to Tools → WebSocket Server Settings
setup.step2Instruction3: Check "Enable WebSocket server" and set the password above
setup.step3Description: Copy this password and paste it in OBS → Tools → WebSocket Server Settings:
setup.addressDescription: Enter the address where OBS is running. Use 'localhost' if OBS is on this computer, or enter an IP address for a remote OBS instance.
setup.noteDescription: Make sure to use the same password in OBS. Church Hub will automatically use this password when connecting.

stream.connectRequired: Connect YouTube or OBS to start streaming

cancelConfirm.title: Cancel Stream Start?

scenes.noScenes: No scenes yet. The setup guide shows how to create the first one.
scenes.useAsStartSceneDescription: This scene will be activated before the stream starts

setup.supportedMixers: Supported mixers: Behringer X32, XR18, XR16, XR12, X-AIR series, and other OSC-compatible mixers.

errors.obsAuthFailed: OBS authentication failed. Check your WebSocket password in OBS settings.
errors.obsTimeout: Connection to OBS timed out. Check that the host and port are correct.
errors.youtubeSessionExpired: Your YouTube session has expired. Please reconnect.
errors.youtubeReauthRequired: YouTube requires you to sign in again
errors.obsNotConnected: OBS is not connected. Please connect to OBS first.

guide.title: Set up your livestream
guide.intro: Do these steps once. After that, Church Hub switches the stream's scenes for you while you present.

obs.title: Connect OBS Studio
obs.install: Install OBS Studio on the computer that streams. It is free, and it sends the camera and Church Hub's text to YouTube.
obs.connect: Then let Church Hub control OBS: in OBS, open Tools → WebSocket Server Settings, turn the server on and use the password from the OBS setup.

browserSource.title: Show Church Hub in OBS
browserSource.description: The Live Stream screen shows the lyrics and Bible verses for the stream, on a transparent background. In OBS, add a Browser source with this address and size:
browserSource.noScreen: There is no Live Stream screen. Add one in Settings → Screens.
browserSource.looks: You choose how the text looks on the Live Stream screen, in Settings → Screens.

firstScene.title: Create your first scene
firstScene.create: In OBS, under Scenes, click + and name the scene exactly “{{name}}”.
firstScene.camera: Under Sources, click + → Video Capture Device and choose your camera.
firstScene.browser: Click + → Browser and add the Church Hub source from step 2, above the camera.
firstScene.others: Make the other scenes below the same way, with the same names. Church Hub finds them as soon as OBS is connected.

switching.title: Switch scenes during the service
switching.click: Click a scene on this page to put it on the stream.
switching.automatic: When you present a song, a Bible verse or an announcement, the stream moves to its scene by itself, and goes back when you hide it. You can rename scenes, hide them or change what switches them.

midi.title: Switch scenes from a MIDI controller
midi.device: Plug in a MIDI pad or keyboard and choose it in Settings → MIDI Controller.
midi.sceneShortcut: Then, in Settings → Live Stream, open a scene, click the shortcut field and press a pad. Starting and stopping the stream can go on pads too, in Settings → Shortcuts.

mixer.title: Connect the audio mixer
mixer.description: With a digital mixer (Behringer X32, XR18 and similar), Church Hub mutes and unmutes channels when the scene changes. Enter the mixer's IP address and turn the control on.

youtube.title: Go live on YouTube
youtube.signIn: Open YouTube settings at the top of the page and connect the church's channel.
youtube.start: Start Stream then creates the broadcast on YouTube and starts OBS; Stop Stream ends it.
youtube.startStopScenes: The stream opens on the “{{start}}” scene and closes on “{{stop}}”.

youtubeSettings.title: YouTube settings
youtubeSettings.subtitle: Every new broadcast is created with these settings.

account.title: YouTube channel
account.description: The channel Church Hub creates the broadcasts on.
account.notConnected: Not connected. Connect the church's channel to set up the broadcasts.

template.title: Start from a previous stream
template.description: Pick a past stream: its title, description, privacy, category, tags, thumbnail and stream settings fill this page. Change what you need, then save.
template.none: No past streams on this channel yet
template.filledFromLatest: Filled in from your latest stream. Check the settings and press Save to keep them.

details.title: Title and description
details.streamTitleHint: A date in the title (16.11.2025, 16 noiembrie 2025) changes to the day of the stream.
details.categoryHint: Helps YouTube show the stream to the right people.
details.tagsHint: Words people might search for, separated by commas.

audience.title: Who can watch
audience.description: Privacy and audience of each new stream.

privacyHint.public: Anyone can find and watch it.
privacyHint.unlisted: Only people with the link can watch it.
privacyHint.private: Only you and the people you invite can watch it.

audience.madeForKidsHint: On only when the stream is made for children. YouTube then turns off comments and the live chat.

stream.title: Stream
stream.description: How the stream reaches YouTube and how it starts and ends.
stream.streamKeyHint: The key set in OBS. The broadcast is tied to it.

latencyHint.normal: Best picture quality; viewers are about 15–30 seconds behind.
latencyHint.low: Viewers are a few seconds behind; good for talking with the chat.
latencyHint.ultraLow: Almost live, at a lower quality; no 1440p or 4K.

stream.dvrHint: Off: viewers always watch live and can't rewind during the stream.
stream.autoStart: Go live when OBS starts streaming
stream.autoStartHint: Off: the stream goes public only when you press Go live in YouTube Studio.
stream.autoStopHint: Off: the broadcast stays open after OBS stops, until Church Hub or YouTube Studio ends it.

extras.title: Thumbnail and playlist
extras.description: Where the stream shows up on the channel.
extras.thumbnailHint: The previous stream's image, set on each new stream. YouTube takes custom thumbnails only from verified channels.
extras.thumbnailNone: No thumbnail: YouTube picks a frame from the stream.
extras.playlistHint: Each new stream is added to this playlist.

chat.title: Live chat and comments
chat.description: Who can write during and after the stream.
chat.notByApi: YouTube doesn't let apps set this. Set it once in YouTube Studio:
chat.stepChat: Live chat for subscribers only: in YouTube Studio open the stream in the Live Control Room, then Edit → Live chat → Who can send messages → Subscribers. On the next stream, "Reuse settings" keeps it.
chat.stepComments: Comments: Settings → Community → Content controls → Comments on new uploads → Hold potentially inappropriate comments for review.

obsSettings.title: OBS settings
obsSettings.subtitle: How Church Hub reaches OBS Studio to start the stream and switch scenes.

connection.title: Connection
connection.description: Church Hub controls OBS through its WebSocket server.
connection.autoConnectHint: Connects to OBS each time Church Hub starts.

access.title: Address and password
access.description: Use the same port and password in OBS → Tools → WebSocket Server Settings.
access.portHint: 4455 unless you changed it in OBS.

mixerSettings.title: Audio mixer settings
mixerSettings.subtitle: The digital mixer Church Hub mutes and unmutes with the scenes.

connection.title: Mixer
connection.enableHint: Off: Church Hub never touches the mixer.
connection.notAnswering: On, but the mixer isn't answering
connection.portHint: 10023 for the X32, 10024 for the XR series.

channels.description: Name the channels so each scene's mute list is easy to read.
